cards.title: Saving water at home
facts: A running tap can waste several litres a minute.
RO purifiers reject a lot of water that can be reused for mopping or plants.
A bucket bath usually uses far less water than a shower.
do: Turn off the tap while brushing
Reuse RO reject water for mopping or plants
Report or fix leaks
Water plants early in the morning
dont: Don't leave taps running
Don't wash vehicles with a running hose

myths.statement: A small dripping tap wastes too little water to matter.
myths.truth: Drips add up to thousands of litres a year. Fix or report it.

quiz.q: Which saves the most water every day?
options: Leaving the tap on while brushing
Turning the tap off while brushing
Washing the car with a hose
quiz.explanation: Small daily habits save a lot over a year.

situations: It's a dry summer in {name}'s city and water comes only twice a day. {At}, {relation} is washing a scooter with a hose that's been running for 20 minutes.
scenario.question: What could {name} suggest?

rubric.point: Use a bucket instead of a running hose
rubric.note: A bucket uses a fraction of the water.

rubric.point: Explain the water shortage kindly
Reuse water (e.g. RO reject) where possible

cards.title: Heat and air quality days
facts: On high-AQI days, hard outdoor exercise means breathing in more pollution.
Burning leaves and waste adds smoke directly to the air.
The hottest part of the day is usually around noon to 3 PM.
do: Check the AQI before outdoor sport
Carry water on hot days
Avoid hard exercise outdoors when AQI is high
Share rides or use public transport
dont: Don't burn leaves or waste
Don't do hard outdoor exercise at midday in a heatwave

myths.statement: If the sky looks clear, the air quality must be good.
myths.truth: Fine particles (PM2.5) are invisible. Check the AQI.

quiz.q: The AQI is 210 today. What's the best choice for sports practice?
options: Move practice indoors or make it light
Burn leaves to clear the air
quiz.explanation: High AQI means more pollution in your lungs during hard exercise.

cards.title: Wet, dry and hazardous waste
facts: Wet waste (food, peels) can be composted.
Batteries and e-waste contain harmful chemicals and need special disposal.
Burning plastic releases toxic fumes.
do: Separate wet, dry and hazardous waste
Compost food scraps if possible
Give e-waste and batteries to collection points
dont: Don't burn plastic
Don't throw batteries in the regular bin

myths.statement: Old batteries can go in the kitchen bin with everything else.
myths.truth: Batteries are hazardous waste. Use e-waste or battery collection points.

quiz.q: Where do banana peels go?
quiz.explanation: Food scraps are wet waste and can be composted.

cards.title: Saving energy at home
facts: Setting the AC to 24–26°C saves a lot of electricity compared with 18–20°C.
Chargers and devices on standby still use some power.
do: Switch off lights and fans when leaving a room
Set AC to 24–26°C
Use daylight when possible
Unplug chargers when done
dont: Don't leave the TV on standby all night
Don't open the fridge door for long

myths.statement: Setting the AC to 16°C cools the room faster.
myths.truth: It cools at the same speed, just longer and colder, using more power. 24–26°C is efficient.

quiz.q: Which AC setting is the most energy-efficient for comfort?
quiz.explanation: 24–26°C is comfortable and saves electricity.

cards.title: Phasing out single-use plastic: Bags, bottles and cutlery
facts: Single-use plastic takes over 450 years to fragment into toxic microscopic plastic particles.
India produces over 3.4 million tonnes of plastic waste annually, choking drainage and marine life.
do: Keep a foldable cloth bag inside your school backpack for unexpected purchases
Carry a reusable steel or copper water bottle instead of buying single-use plastic bottles
Refuse plastic straws, spoons, and disposable plastic carry bags politely: 'I brought my own'
dont: Never burn plastic waste in the open (releases carcinogenic dioxins and furans)
Never throw plastic packets into gutters or open plots

myths.statement: Thin plastic carry bags dissolve quickly in sunlight and soil.
myths.truth: Plastics never biodegrade; they merely fragment into toxic microplastics that enter our drinking water and food.

quiz.q: What is the simplest daily habit to stop plastic waste at the market?
options: Carry your own washable cloth tote bag and steel bottle
quiz.explanation: Carrying a reusable bag eliminates hundreds of single-use plastic bags per person every year.

situations: At the neighborhood grocery shop at {at}, the vendor offers {name} three thin black plastic carry bags.
scenario.question: What eco-friendly action should {name} take?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely refuse the plastic bags: 'No thank you, I have a cloth bag'
rubric.keys: refuse plastic|use cloth bag|brought my own

rubric.point: Use a reusable cloth tote or backpack to pack items
Explain gently to peers why single-use plastics choke city drains

cards.title: Safe disposal of electronic waste (e-waste) and old batteries
facts: Discarded electronics contain toxic heavy metals: lead, mercury, cadmium, and arsenic.
Tossing batteries into common garbage contaminates local municipal soil and groundwater aquifers.
do: Deposit old mobile phones, chargers, and wires at authorized e-waste collection bins
Look for certified take-back programs at electronics retail stores and schools
Store swollen or leaking batteries in a fire-safe container before dropping at recycling centers
dont: Never throw discarded gadgets, wires, or batteries into normal household dustbins
Never dismantle or break open old cathode ray tubes or lithium-ion batteries

myths.statement: Old mobile phones thrown into landfills safely rust away like iron nails.
myths.truth: Batteries and circuit boards leach lethal heavy metals like cadmium and lead into drinking wells.

quiz.q: Where should you deposit broken earphones, old tablets, and dead batteries?
options: At an authorized e-waste collection center or brand take-back bin
quiz.explanation: Certified e-waste recyclers dismantle electronics in vacuum-sealed facilities to recover gold and copper safely.

situations: Cleaning out a study desk drawer at {at}, {name} finds three dead mobile batteries and tangled broken chargers.
scenario.question: What is the ecologically responsible way to discard them?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Collect them in a box and take them to an authorized e-waste drop-off bin
rubric.note: Prevents hazardous heavy metal soil contamination.

rubric.point: Do not throw electronics into daily municipal garbage dustbins
rubric.note: Protects waste pickers from toxic exposure.
rubric.keys: don'?t throw in trash|no daily dustbin

rubric.point: Check if local electronics stores or schools have e-waste drives

cards.title: Kitchen wet waste composting: Turning peels into black gold
facts: Over 50% of urban household waste is organic wet waste (fruit peels, vegetable stalks, tea leaves).
When organic matter rots under plastic in landfills without oxygen, it generates methane, a potent greenhouse gas.
do: Segregate wet green waste (fruit peels, vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells)
Mix greens with dry brown waste (dry leaves, shredded cardboard, sawdust) in a ventilated pot
Turn the compost pile once a week to let aerobic bacteria create rich, odor-free garden soil
dont: Never add plastic wrappers, foil, dairy, cooked oils, or meat bones to basic home compost
Never let the compost pile become waterlogged and smelly

myths.statement: Composting at home always produces terrible foul smells and attracts thousands of flies.
myths.truth: A balanced compost pile with proper brown leaves and aeration smells like fresh forest soil.

quiz.q: What two types of waste must be balanced in a home compost bin to keep it healthy?
options: Nitrogen-rich 'Greens' (kitchen peels) and Carbon-rich 'Browns' (dry leaves, cardboard)
quiz.explanation: A 1:2 ratio of wet green peels to dry brown leaves creates ideal aerobic decomposition.

situations: At home at {at}, {name} notices daily vegetable cuttings and banana peels being thrown into the trash bin.
scenario.question: How can {name} start simple kitchen waste composting?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Collect fruit and vegetable peels in a separate 'Wet Waste' bin
Layer the wet peels with dry garden leaves or crushed paper in a terracotta pot
Harvest rich dark organic compost in 60-90 days for house plants

sources.name: Swachh Bharat Mission Solid Waste Management Rules

cards.title: Planting and caring for native shade trees (Neem, Peepal, Jamun)
facts: Native Indian trees (Neem, Peepal, Banyan, Jamun) support hundreds of local birds and pollinators.
Exotic trees (like Eucalyptus and Conocarpus) deplete groundwater and provide zero food for native biodiversity.
do: Plant indigenous native species adapted to local rainfall: Neem, Amla, Jamun, Peepal, Amaltas
Water newly planted saplings deeply twice a week during their first two summers
Protect young saplings with bamboo tree guards against grazing goats and cattle
dont: Never plant invasive water-guzzling exotic species near groundwater wells
Never plant trees and abandon them without water in peak summer

myths.statement: Planting any tree anywhere helps the environment equally, even exotic ornamental species.
myths.truth: Exotic monocultures destroy local bird nesting ecosystems. Always plant native indigenous species.

quiz.q: Why are native Indian trees like Neem and Jamun far superior to exotic ornamental trees?
options: They conserve groundwater, provide fruits for local birds, and thrive in Indian heat
quiz.explanation: Native trees have evolved with Indian soil, supporting bees, birds, and natural groundwater retention.

situations: During a school plantation drive at {at}, {name} is selecting saplings for the campus grounds.
scenario.question: What wise ecological choices should {name} make?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Choose native Indian tree saplings like Neem, Jamun, Peepal, or Amaltas
rubric.note: Thrives naturally and feeds local urban wildlife.

rubric.point: Commit to regular watering and weeding for the sapling's first two years
Mulch around the base with dry leaves to retain soil moisture

cards.title: Stubble and dry leaf burning: Toxic air and soil degradation
facts: Burning crop residue or dry leaves releases dense clouds of carbon monoxide, PM2.5, and black carbon.
Ground fires incinerate beneficial earthworms, mycorrhizal fungi, and organic soil carbon.
do: Compost dry leaves and autumn garden clippings instead of lighting them on fire
Advocate for happy-seeders, bio-decomposers, and mulching instead of open crop stubble burning
Report open garbage or leaf burning fires to municipal pollution ward helplines
dont: Never light fires to clear backyard dry leaves or park trimmings
Never burn municipal trash or plastic in roadside piles

myths.statement: Burning dry leaves in winter is a harmless way to clear colony gardens and get warm.
myths.truth: Leaf burning releases hazardous carcinogenic smoke directly into children's and elders' breathing zones.

quiz.q: What happens to the soil when garden leaves or crop stubble are burned on the ground?
options: Intense heat kills beneficial earthworms, microbes, and destroys soil moisture
quiz.explanation: Fire sterilizes topsoil, destroying organic nitrogen and beneficial microbial life.

situations: In the neighborhood park at {at}, a gardener is sweeping dry leaves into a pile and preparing to light a match.
scenario.question: How should {name} intervene respectfully?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely request the gardener not to burn the leaves: 'Burning releases toxic smoke into our lungs'
Suggest composting the leaves in a park pit to create free natural plant manure
Remind that open burning in cities is prohibited by the National Green Tribunal (NGT)

cards.title: Preventing urban waterlogging: Stormwater drains vs garbage
facts: Stormwater drains are designed solely to channel monsoon rainwater away into natural water bodies.
Plastic bags, gutkha packets, and construction debris clog drain grates, creating flash urban floods.
do: Keep street stormwater drain grates clean and free of discarded snack packets
Dispose of household garbage exclusively via door-to-door municipal collection vans
Report choked colony drains to the municipal corporation before monsoon season begins
dont: Never sweep street dust, leaves, or plastic wrappers into storm drain openings
Never dump construction debris (malba) into roadside storm gutters

myths.statement: Stormwater drains are underground trash shoots that automatically wash garbage away.
myths.truth: Solid waste accumulates at culvert bends, completely choking stormwater flow and flooding roads.

quiz.q: Why do Indian cities experience sudden knee-deep road flooding after only 30 minutes of rain?
options: Stormwater drains are choked with single-use plastics, silt, and dumped garbage
quiz.explanation: Blocked drain gratings prevent heavy runoff from entering drainage networks.

situations: Walking past a colony storm drain grating at {at}, {name} sees it choked with discarded plastic wrappers.
scenario.question: What proactive civic actions prevent monsoon waterlogging?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Clear surface plastic wrappers away from the drain grate with a stick or gloves
Throw discarded wrappers into the nearest dry waste bin
Educate neighbours never to use storm drains as trash cans

cards.title: Rooftop rainwater harvesting: Recharging groundwater
facts: Concrete roads and paved yards prevent rainwater from percolating into underground aquifers.
A 100 sq meter rooftop in a city with 800mm annual rain can harvest over 60,000 litres of clean water.
do: Filter rooftop rainwater through sand and gravel layers to recharge colony borewells
Store harvested rainwater in clean underground tanks for gardening and toilet flushing
Keep rooftop catchments clean and inspect first-flush pipe diverters before monsoon
dont: Never let pristine rooftop monsoon rain run off into dirty sewage gutters
Never connect sewage lines into groundwater recharge pits

myths.statement: Rainwater harvesting is only useful for huge rural farms, not city apartment buildings.
myths.truth: Urban rooftop rainwater harvesting directly recharges dry borewells and prevents city floods.

quiz.q: What happens when rainwater from building rooftops is routed into groundwater recharge pits?
options: It recharges depleted subterranean water tables and revives drying wells
quiz.explanation: Percolation pits channel clean rainwater deep into permeable soil layers, raising the water table.

situations: {name}'s school or residential building at {at} experiences dry borewells every summer.
scenario.question: How can rooftop rainwater harvesting solve this water crisis?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Channel clean rooftop rainwater into a filtration chamber and percolation recharge pit
Use first-flush diverters to wash away initial roof dust and debris
rubric.note: Ensures only clean rainwater enters recharge wells.

rubric.point: Save thousands of litres of water for secondary non-potable uses

dangerous: let all rain wash into sewage

cards.title: Saving paper: Using both sides, digital notes and recycling
facts: Producing 1 tonne of virgin paper consumes approximately 17 mature trees and 26,000 litres of water.
Using both sides of every notebook page cuts individual classroom paper footprint by 50%.
do: Use every single page of your school notebooks from top margin to bottom margin
Bind leftover blank pages from old school notebooks into rough work practice pads
Donate used textbooks to junior students or school book banks for multi-year reuse
dont: Never tear out blank notebook pages to make paper planes or doodles
Never throw whole paper notebooks into the wet garbage bin

myths.statement: Tearing out pages from school notebooks doesn't hurt trees because paper comes from shops.
myths.truth: Every sheet of virgin paper represents felled pulp trees, heavy water consumption, and bleaching chemicals.

quiz.q: What is the best way to reuse notebooks with 20-30 blank leftover pages at the end of the school year?
options: Carefully bind the blank sheets together to create a rough practice notebook
quiz.explanation: Binding unused blank pages creates free rough pads and saves trees from being cut.

situations: At the end of the school term at {at}, {name} has three half-filled notebooks with 40 clean blank pages each.
scenario.question: What is the eco-friendly way to use these pages?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Tear out or bind the unused pages together to make a rough work pad for homework
rubric.note: Maximizes paper utility to the last sheet.
rubric.keys: reuse blank pages|make rough pad|bind pages

rubric.point: Pass on clean textbooks to junior classmates through a book bank
rubric.note: Extends textbook lifespan across multiple students.

rubric.point: Send completely filled pages to certified paper recycling vendors
rubric.note: Recycled pulp saves trees and water.

cards.title: Repair and reuse culture: Fixing before throwing away
facts: Modern 'throwaway culture' drives excessive resource mining, industrial manufacturing, and waste heaps.
Repairing shoes, stitching bags, and replacing appliance parts supports local repair artisans and saves money.
do: Take torn school backpacks or broken umbrella ribs to local cobblers and tailors for repair
Upgrade or repair computer RAM/storage before buying a completely new device
Organize a toy, game, or book swap meet with friends instead of buying new items
dont: Never throw away repairable gadgets or bags just to buy the latest trendy model
Never treat items as disposable after minor tears or scuffs

myths.statement: Buying a brand-new backpack every school year is necessary even if your old bag only has a stuck zipper.
myths.truth: A local tailor can replace a zipper slider for ₹20 in 5 minutes, saving thousands of rupees and manufacturing waste.

quiz.q: What is the most sustainable option when a zipper gets stuck on your favourite school bag?
options: Take it to a local tailor or cobbler to replace the zipper runner
quiz.explanation: Repairing items honors craftspeople, saves family money, and prevents landfill waste.

situations: The zipper on {name}'s sturdy school backpack splits open at {at}.
scenario.question: How does {name} practice circular economy thinking?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Visit a local neighborhood tailor or bag repair artisan to fix the zipper slider
rubric.note: Extends product lifespan by years for minimal cost.

rubric.point: Understand that repairing items conserves raw materials and fossil energy
Wash and maintain the backpack to keep it fresh for another school term

cards.title: Switching off vehicle engines at red traffic lights
facts: Idling a car engine for over 10 seconds consumes more fuel than restarting the engine.
Vehicle exhaust at idling intersections creates concentrated toxic plumes of benzene and PM2.5 at children's eye level.
do: Ask family drivers to switch off the engine at traffic signals with countdown timers over 15 seconds
Turn off vehicles while waiting outside school pick-up gates or railway crossings
Walking or cycling for short neighborhood errands under 1 km saves fuel and emissions
dont: Never leave car air-conditioners running while idling parked for 20 minutes outside shops
Never rev engines aggressively while waiting at red lights

myths.statement: Stopping and restarting your car engine at red lights damages the starter motor and wastes more petrol.
myths.truth: Modern vehicle starters are designed for thousands of cycles; idling for 10 seconds wastes far more fuel.

quiz.q: At what traffic signal countdown time is it scientifically proven to save fuel by switching off the engine?
options: Only if red light is 1 hour
If the red light timer is longer than 15-20 seconds
quiz.explanation: Switching off at signals over 15 seconds cuts tailpipe emissions and saves litres of fuel monthly.

situations: Waiting in a car or auto at a 90-second red light signal at {at}, the engine is idling noisily.
scenario.question: What polite green tip can {name} share with the driver?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely suggest: 'Uncle/Papa, the light is 90 seconds, switching off the engine saves fuel and air'
rubric.note: Saves fuel and cuts street-level emissions.
rubric.keys: switch off engine|red light|save fuel|clean air

rubric.point: Explain that restarting modern vehicles uses less fuel than 10 seconds of idling
Notice how turning off the engine reduces noise and vibration inside the vehicle

cards.title: Summer water bowls for urban birds and street animals
facts: Urbanization, asphalt, and concrete drain covers eliminate natural puddles and drinking ponds for city birds.
During scorching Indian summers (40°C+), hundreds of sparrows, pigeons, and squirrels die of dehydration.
do: Place wide, shallow terracotta clay bowls filled with fresh water on balconies, terraces, and gardens
Keep water bowls in the shade to prevent water from becoming burning hot under midday sun
Wash and refill the bowl daily with clean water to prevent mosquito larvae from breeding
dont: Never leave dirty, stagnant green slime water in bowls (breeds dengue mosquitoes)
Never use deep slick plastic buckets where small birds can fall in and drown

myths.statement: Leaving a water bowl outside once a month is enough for birds in May.
myths.truth: Shallow water evaporates in hours during peak summer. Daily cleaning and refilling are vital.

quiz.q: What material is best for an outdoor bird water bowl?
options: A wide, shallow unglazed terracotta clay dish (keeps water naturally cool)
quiz.explanation: Porous terracotta allows gentle evaporation, keeping water refreshingly cool for birds.

situations: During intense May summer heat at {at}, {name} sees panting sparrows and squirrels on the balcony railing.
scenario.question: How can {name} provide immediate life-saving relief?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Set out a wide, shallow clay saucer filled with fresh water in a shady spot
rubric.note: Quenches dehydration safely without drowning hazard.

rubric.point: Wash and replace the water daily to keep it hygienic and mosquito-free
Scatter a few grains of millets, rice, or seeds nearby

dangerous: use deep bucket where birds drown

cards.title: Noise pollution impact on urban birds, pets and nocturnal wildlife
facts: Birds use acoustic song frequencies for territory defense, mating calls, and predator danger alarms.
Urban traffic rumble and festive firecrackers force songbirds to shout, disorienting their navigation.
do: Keep festival celebrations green with lights and flowers instead of deafening explosive crackers
Keep household pets indoors in a quiet, sheltered room with closed curtains during loud celebrations
Support city silence zones around bird sanctuaries, zoological parks, and forested urban ridges
dont: Never burst loud firecrackers near trees, nesting colonies, or animal shelters
Never play blaring DJ music in eco-sensitive zones or national parks

myths.statement: Street birds and stray animals do not mind loud chemical firecrackers at all.
myths.truth: Dogs hear acoustic frequencies 4 times higher than humans; explosions cause severe panic, tremors, and cardiac arrest.

quiz.q: Why do birds abandon city gardens exposed to continuous loud construction and traffic noise?
options: Noise masks their mating calls, alarm songs, and acoustic predator alerts
quiz.explanation: Acoustic masking prevents avian communication, forcing bird populations to flee noisy cities.

situations: During festival night at {at}, neighbours are preparing to burst high-decibel aerial firecrackers near park trees.
scenario.question: What compassionate wildlife awareness can {name} champion?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Celebrate with beautiful earthen diyas, lanterns, and sweets instead of loud crackers
Explain that loud acoustic blasts cause terror and disorientation in nesting birds and pets
rubric.note: Builds empathy for non-human urban residents.

rubric.point: Provide a quiet, safe corner inside for frightened domestic pets during celebrations

cards.title: Understanding the Air Quality Index (AQI) and protecting lungs
facts: The AQI measures 8 major pollutants, with fine PM2.5 (particles 30 times thinner than hair) being the most lethal.
When AQI exceeds 300 ('Severe'), breathing outdoor air for a day equals smoking 15-20 cigarettes.
do: Check your city's daily AQI on government apps (Sameer app by CPCB) before outdoor morning sports
Wear an authentic, well-fitted N95 or FFP2 particulate mask when AQI enters 'Very Poor' (300+) levels
Shift strenuous aerobic sports indoors during severe smog inversion episodes
dont: Never rely on thin cloth handkerchiefs or surgical masks (they filter 0% of micro PM2.5 particles)
Never do heavy outdoor sprint workouts in dense winter smog

myths.statement: Wrapping a cotton handkerchief around your mouth blocks all dangerous air pollution.
myths.truth: Cotton cloth weaves have pore gaps thousands of times larger than PM2.5 particles. Only certified N95 masks filter them.

quiz.q: What official government mobile app provides real-time AQI readings for Indian cities?
options: SAMEER App by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
quiz.explanation: The SAMEER app provides hour-by-hour air quality monitoring from CPCB observation towers across India.

situations: On a cold winter morning at {at}, the city AQI reads 380 ('Severe / Hazardous') on the weather app.
scenario.question: How should {name} adjust daily activities to safeguard lung health?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wear a certified, snug-fitting N95 mask if stepping outdoors
Reschedule heavy outdoor running or football to indoor light stretches
rubric.note: Prevents deep inhalation of toxic smog.
rubric.keys: indoor exercise|avoid heavy outdoor sports|severe aqi

rubric.point: Check the CPCB SAMEER app daily to monitor air quality trends

cards.title: Climate change explained simply: Greenhouse gases and solutions

myths.statement: Climate change is a fictional theory that only affects polar bears in the Arctic.

quiz.q: What primary human activity drives accelerated global climate change?
options: Burning fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) releasing greenhouse gases
quiz.explanation: Fossil fuel combustion releases billions of tonnes of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

cards.title: Celebrating festivals green: Clay idols, herbal colors and zero plastic

myths.statement: Plaster of Paris (PoP) dissolves harmlessly in rivers just like natural river clay.

quiz.q: Why are natural clay (Shadu Mati) idols vastly superior to Plaster of Paris (PoP) statues?

quiz.explanation: Pure clay returns to nature organically without poisoning municipal water supply sources.

Never spray toxic chemical insecticides on flowering garden plants

myths.statement: Cities have zero biodiversity; you must visit deep national forest reserves to see living nature.
myths.truth: Indian city trees host tailorbirds, bulObjective, barbets, honeybees, and diverse pollinator ecosystems.

quiz.q: What is the ecological term for observing and recording living species in your immediate neighborhood?
quiz.explanation: Citizen science empowers everyday students to document local species and preserve urban nature.
